ANSWER: In `src/memory/guard.rs`:

- **`secret_kind`** (line 53) is the function that decides whether a piece of text looks like a secret. It first checks the text against a set of named regex patterns (private keys, AWS keys, GitHub tokens, API keys, etc.). If none match, it then scans for any long token (32+ chars of `[A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]`) and calls **`looks_random`** on each match.

- **`looks_random`** (line 62) is the helper that distinguishes high-entropy base64 keys from hex hashes and IDs. It requires the token to have mixed case (both upper and lower) plus digits, then computes Shannon entropy over the byte distribution — returning `true` (i.e., "looks like a secret") only if entropy exceeds 4.2 bits per character. Hex strings and base32 IDs, which lack mixed case, fail the first check and pass through safely.

CONFIDENCE: high
